label: Strength and performance, not measured muscle growth
model_note: Trends, stalls and wins come from what was logged (loads, reps, hold times, RIR). They describe strength and performance, are modelled, and are not a measurement of muscle growth. No medical or injury advice.
focus: Progress first (motivation), then stalls to adjust. Planned vs done is a minor footnote only.

units.display: history.settings.unit (lb default); loads are stored in each session's unit and converted for display only

effort.store: set.rir = integer 0..4 (4 means 4+) or null when not logged. Only RIR is stored.
effort.rpe_toggle: history.settings.effort = "rir" (default) | "rpe". Display and input only: RPE = 10 - RIR. Chips 10, 9, 8, 7, <=6; <=6 stores RIR 4. No half points.
effort.legacy_read: on read: values above 4 clamp to 4 (legacy 5+ -> 4); fractional values round to the nearest integer (half up: 1.5 -> 2); negatives clamp to 0; anything non-numeric -> null
effort.summary: average RIR per muscle over the last 28 days, stimulus-weighted: sum(rating x rir) / sum(rating) over done working sets with RIR logged, rating = exercises.json muscle ratio >= 0.25; 4+ counts as 4; deload sessions excluded. Fewer than 6 such sets -> not shown ("not enough RIR logged").
effort.far_from_failure_note: Sets ended about {avg} reps from failure on average. Sets this far from failure may explain part of the stall.
effort.hard_set_link: Hard set = done working set with RIR <= logger.hardRIR (3) or no RIR logged (logging-spec §5). A 4+ set is never a hard set, so the far-from-failure line (average >= 3) sits at the edge of the hard-set rule: the same number, read the same way.

e1rm.sets: done working sets with 1..12 reps; warm-ups excluded; set tags per logger.set_tags.pr_exclude (e1rm); effective load (bodyweight share included) as prs.flatten
e1rm.note: Estimated 1RM by the Epley formula, a model, not a tested max. Cap raised from 10 to 12 reps by Chief of Staff (2026-10-24); accuracy falls as reps rise.
e1rm.rules_json: rules.json logger.e1rm_max_reps = 12 since progress3 (Chief of Staff, Oct 24, 2026): PR badges (prs.py), Log charts, Train and Progress all cap at 12

metrics.load_index: best load x (1 + reps / 30) over all working sets, any rep count: the Epley shape used as a trend index for high-rep, core and carry lifts; never shown or named as a 1RM
metrics.reps: most reps in one working set

hold.when: swap.flags has static_hold, or the whiteboard rep range unit is seconds
hold.value: longest hold (set.reps holds seconds for these exercises)

distance.when: whiteboard rep range unit is meters (carries)
distance.value: load-reps index with meters in place of reps (set.reps holds meters)

bodyweight.when: exercises.json bodyweight_fraction > 0 (bodyweight, rings, suspension, assisted machines)
bodyweight.value: most reps in one working set; added load (or assistance) compared separately

core.when: primary muscle (highest rating) is abs or obliques
core.value: load-reps index (no load ever logged -> metric reps)

e1rm.value: best estimated 1RM per session (Epley, sets <= 12 reps)
e1rm.high_rep_fallback: if any of the lift's non-deload sessions in the 3-month dashboard window (all its sessions if none there) has no done working set of <= 12 reps (e.g. calf raises at 12-20, curls at 10-15), its metric is load_index instead, for the lift card and the dashboard alike, so a lift never mixes estimated 1RM points and gaps

lift_kinds.bodyweight_trend: bodyweight lifts trend, stall and dropping on reps only across sessions at the latest session's added load (within half a step; bodyweight-only sessions have added load 0); a heavier added load is a gain, not a drop in reps

comparable.rule: the previous completed, non-deload session that logged the same exercise id (aliases resolved) within the last 56 days
comparable.top_set: heaviest logged (added) load among done working sets; hold lifts: longest hold
comparable.same_load: within half the smallest real load step (prs.step_kg, gym profile aware)
comparable.gain: load up by more than half a step; or same load and more reps in the best set at that load; or same best-set reps and the same number of sets at that load with more total reps; hold lifts: longer hold

texts.none: No comparable session in the last 56 days

weekly_best.value: best metric of the week (estimated 1RM for e1rm lifts); deload sessions excluded
weekly_best.pr_week: the week best is above every earlier week best by more than review.flat_pct (1%) (reps / hold: strictly more); the first logged week is the baseline, never a PR week

trend.method: least-squares slope of the weekly best metric vs week index over weeks with data in the window, as % of the mean per week

lift_status.stalled: the last >= 3 exposures (non-deload) brought no rep/load gain over the best exposure before them (gain rule above); needs >= 4 exposures and >= 21 days of data
lift_status.decline: an exposure that is not a gain over the reference exposure and whose metric is more than review.flat_pct (1%) below it
lift_status.dropping: the last 2 exposures are both declines vs the recent best (the best of the 3 exposures before them): 2 sessions in a row below it, as logging-spec §9 performance drop; catches step-wise drops (down, same, down); needs >= 4 exposures

muscle.credit: exercises with an exercises.json rating >= 0.25 for the muscle
muscle.weight: stimulus share = credited hard sets in the window (rating x hard sets), same counting as targets.json
muscle.trend: weighted mean of the %/week of its lifts that have a trend; same thresholds as lifts
muscle.min_data: at least one lift with a trend and >= 3 distinct weeks with a credited set in the window
muscle.main_lift: pinned (history.settings.mainLiftPins[muscle], must credit the muscle >= 0.25) else the lift with the most sessions in the window among lifts rated >= 0.5 (none: >= 0.25); ties: higher rating, more credited sets, primary < accessory < isolation, id
muscle.latest_gain: the main lift's change vs its last comparable session
muscle.stuck: muscle trend is flat or down AND its main lift is stalled or dropping AND lifts that are stalled or dropping carry >= 50% of the muscle's weight

deload.one_rule: There is one deload rule: logger.deload_signals points (tools/deload.py deload_check: eligibility, weeks since deload, RIR drift, hard sets over target, readiness, suggest_score 3), with its performance signal REPLACED by the Progress lift statuses below. Progress, Train and Log all use it: rules.json logger.deload_signals.performance = {"source": "progress-rules.json#deload", ...inline values} since progress3, and tools/deload.py deload_check calls tools/progress.py perf_signal.

several_lifts_dropping.rule: >= 2 lifts with status dropping whose latest exposure is in the last 14 days

mostly_stalled.rule: otherwise, >= 3 lifts with a status and >= 60% of them stalled or dropping

deload.apply_note: a deload is a temporary week overlay (logging-spec §9); the board is not changed

rules.deload: the deload is suggested (see deload.one_rule): it then becomes the only needs-attention item and covers every stall and drop
rules.sets_up: mean credited hard sets of the muscle over the last 2 completed weeks < targets.json min x levelMinFactor (rounded to 0.5): +1 set on the lift (first routine day that has it)
rules.sets_down: that mean > targets.json max: -1 set on the lift (never below 2)
rules.swap: the stall has lasted >= 6 exposures: swap the lift for the first swap.py candidate in the same equipment family that fits its template slot and is not already in the routine (none: next rule)
rules.rep_range: otherwise: move to the other half of the lift's rep range for a while (top-set reps at or below the middle -> upper half, else lower half)

fix.can_apply_note: can_apply = Apply edits the board (analysis ops sets / swap, with Undo). Deload is a week overlay; rep-range advice is display only until the board has a rep-range op.

needs_attention.order: deload first, then muscle stalls (main lift stall length desc, muscle order), then dropping lifts not already shown as a stalled muscle's main lift (latest drop first)
needs_attention.grouping: stuck muscles that share a main lift make one item (muscles listed together, one fix)
needs_attention.deload_absorbs: when the deload is suggested it is the only item: it lists the stuck muscles and dropping lifts it covers (their one fix would be the deload anyway)

wins.baseline: the first session with an exercise sets its baseline: no win from it
wins.e1rm_pr: best estimated 1RM above every earlier one by more than review.flat_pct (1%) (e1rm lifts)
wins.strongest_ever: an estimated 1RM PR that is still the all-time best at as_of, on a lift with >= 28 days of history: shown as "Strongest ever"
wins.load_pr: heaviest logged load above every earlier one by more than half a step (e1rm, core, distance lifts; bodyweight lifts with added load)
wins.rep_pr: more reps in one working set than ever at that load or heavier (earlier sets within half a step count as the same load); bodyweight lifts with no added load: more reps than ever

milestone.rule: first done working set with >= 1 rep at a logged load >= the milestone (session unit; kg sessions use plates_kg), after the baseline session

vs_3_months.rule: the dashboard change (best of the first 14 days of the 91-day window vs best of the last 14 days; estimated 1RM, load-reps index, best reps at bodyweight or best hold); shown as a win only if >= +1% and the lift has no other win in the list

wins.dedupe: one win per lift per session (highest kind); then one win per lift in the list (best kind, newest); vs_3_months only for lifts with no other win, at most 2
wins.sort: kind rank, then lifts that are some muscle's main lift first, then exercise type (primary, accessory, isolation), then date (newest first), then gain % (desc), then exercise id

dashboard.note: Progress dashboard (KPI strip, body map, muscle table, win chips, dot charts). Strength and performance, not measured muscle growth. Every threshold is a modelling choice [M].
dashboard.window: 3 months = the 91 days ending at as_of (as_of - 90 .. as_of), local dates; deload sessions never count

metric.rule: one dashboard value per lift session, by lift kind: e1rm lifts -> estimated 1RM (Epley, sets <= 12 reps); core / carry / high-rep lifts -> load_index; bodyweight lifts -> best_reps; hold lifts -> best hold (s); core lifts with no load -> best_reps
metric.best_reps: most reps in one done working set at bodyweight (added load within half a load step of 0); weighted and assisted sets are left out of Best reps (they still count for load PRs and hard sets). A session with no bodyweight set has no Best reps value.
metric.weighted_variants: a bodyweight lift logged only with added load (e.g. weighted dips) has no Best reps in the window: change and band are insufficient ("weighted sets only"); its progress shows as load PRs. No bodyweight-included 1RM is shown.

change.early: best dashboard value in the first 14 days of the window that has this lift: from its first non-deload session in the window (s) to s + 13
change.late: best dashboard value in the last 14 days (as_of - 13 .. as_of)
change.weeks: (as_of - 13 - s) / 7, the gap between the two 14-day periods
change.min_data: >= 4 non-deload sessions in the window, a value in both periods, and s <= as_of - 56 (>= 8 weeks of data, so the periods are >= 30 days apart)
change.round: stored to 2 decimals; shown to the nearest 0.5% from 1% up, one decimal below 1% (e.g. "+12.5%", "+0.8%")

band.rule: per muscle, from its main lift's change pct_per_week (the same number as the table change %, divided by the weeks between the periods)
band.thresholds: up_strong > +1.5 %/week; up > +0.5; down < -1.0; flat = -1.0 .. +0.5 inclusive (the flat band). Up and down are the 42-day trend thresholds (logger.progress_signals), applied to the 3-month change rate.
band.stall_marker: a muscle with the stall flag (muscle.stuck) keeps its band colour and gets the attention marker (outline / dot); the KPI counts it as stalled or dropping
band.not_trained: muscles with no lift crediting them (rating >= 0.25) in the window: not coloured, not counted

strength_change.lifts: unique main lifts of the trained muscles (a lift that is main for several muscles counts once) whose dashboard metric is e1rm or load_index and whose change has enough data
strength_change.value: median of those lifts' change pct (even count: mean of the middle two)
strength_change.why: Median over unique lifts: one new or fast-moving lift (e.g. a lift added late or recovering from a break) cannot swing it, and a lift that is main for four muscles (deadlift) is not counted four times. A mean weighted by stimulus would mostly repeat the biggest compound lifts. Best reps and hold changes are left out: their percentages run on a different scale (one more rep at 10 reps is +10%, about +3% estimated 1RM), so mixing them would inflate the median. They show in the table and in vs 3 months ago instead.
strength_change.label: Strength change vs 3 months ago
strength_change.sublabel: Median of main lifts (estimated 1RM, or the load-reps index for high-rep lifts). Strength and performance, not measured muscle growth.
strength_change.round: nearest 0.5% from 1% up, one decimal below 1%

muscle_counts.rule: trained muscles only. stalled_or_dropping = muscle stall flag (muscle.stuck) OR band down (the stall flag has its own minimum data, so a stalled muscle counts here even when its 3-month band is insufficient); else progressing = band up_strong or up; else flat = band flat; else (band insufficient) not in a bucket, shown as the insufficient count.

prs_30d.rule: wins events (same PR definitions as wins: estimated 1RM PR on sets <= 12 reps, load PR, rep PR at a weight, hold PR, plate milestone, strongest ever) dated in the last 30 days (as_of - 29 .. as_of); one per lift per session (highest kind); vs 3 months ago is not a PR
prs_30d.label: PRs, last 30 days
prs_30d.audit: progress4 check (2026-10-24): no inflation from rep PRs at many weights. Events are already one per lift per session (highest kind), and a rep PR is reported once per session at the heaviest weight that beat the earlier best reps at that weight or heavier. On the sample all 54 rep PRs in the last 30 days are top-weight sets and also new plotted bests; the count is high because double progression gives a rep PR almost every session. Count kept unchanged.

avg_rir.rule: plain mean of logged RIR over done working sets in the last 28 days (as_of - 27 .. as_of), deload sessions left out; 4+ counts as 4; sets with no RIR are skipped; each set counts once. Same pool, window and minimum as the per-muscle effort.avg_rir (which weights each set by muscle rating); rounded to 1 decimal
avg_rir.share_logged: logged_sets / eligible_sets, where eligible = every done working set in the same pool, RIR logged or not
avg_rir.partial_note: Based on the {n} of {total} sets with RIR logged
avg_rir.label: Average RIR, last 28 days

table.change_pct: the main lift's change pct (dashboard.change); same main lift as the muscle cards (pinned, else most sessions in the 42-day window)

sparkline.rule: the main lift's weekly best dashboard value for the 12 Monday-to-Sunday weeks ending with the week of as_of, oldest first; null for weeks with no value (deload-only weeks also null, flagged)
sparkline.why: one lift's own number (estimated 1RM, reps or hold) is easy to read and matches the change %; a combined muscle index would need weights and units nobody can check

dots.dot: one per session with the lift: the session's best set as its dashboard value (estimated 1RM, load-reps index, best reps or best hold)
dots.pr: dot.pr = true when that session has a wins event for the lift (any PR kind); used for event chips and tooltips, not for the chart marker
dots.best: dot.best = true only when the dot's plotted value (dot.value, as stored) is strictly higher than every earlier dot value of that lift, over all history (not only the window shown); the lift's first-ever session and deload dots are false. The chart marker uses best
dots.deload: deload sessions are shown as hollow dots (dot.deload = true) and never counted as PRs or in trends

dashboard.vs_3_months: wins vs 3 months ago uses this change for every lift with enough data, including bodyweight lifts (best reps) and hold lifts (best hold)

min_data.lift_trend: 3 exposures in >= 3 weeks spanning >= 14 days (42-day window)
min_data.muscle_trend: 1 lift with a trend and >= 3 weeks with credited sets
min_data.deload: logger.deload_signals.eligible (>= 4 logged weeks, >= 8 sessions, >= 4 weeks since the last deload)
min_data.wins: a baseline session per lift; vs 3 months needs data in both windows

footnote.planned_vs_done: minor footnote only: planned working sets (session snapshots) vs done planned sets, completed and skipped sessions of the last 28 days
footnote.text: Planned vs done, last 4 weeks: {done} of {planned} sets

text_rules: Plain words. Model language ("about", "estimated"). No medical, health or injury claims. No claims about muscle growth from these numbers.
